name: The Contemporary Austin
funding: Expenses $10.3M (2024); trustees, members, Still Water Foundation, and Suzanne Deal Booth with FLAG Art Foundation for the prize.
watch: No excluded name on its board. No controversy found.
records_note: Its Form 990s for 2000 to 2024 are on ProPublica, its archived About page names 36 trustees, and event pages name sponsors; no annual report found.

name: The Dowse Art Museum
funding: Mostly funded by Hutt City Council, plus the Dowse Foundation; Jan 2025 archive names Dulux as a corporate partner and Steel & Tube as a donor.
watch: Dulux is named as one of its corporate partners.
records_note: A council museum: its Foundation site names supporters and trustees but posts no reports. The museum and council sites were blocked.

name: The Drawing Center
funding: $3.5M expenses (2023); Toll family, Warhol/Mellon/Frankenthaler foundations, NYC DCLA and NYSCA, galleries, UNIQLO.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies is in the top donor tier (Jul 2023-Jan 2025). In 2005 Gov. Pataki pushed it out of the Ground Zero site over its programming.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, the donors page names $1,000+ donors to January 2025, and the board is listed.

name: The Freedom Theatre
funding: 2013 annual report names Ford Foundation, Sida, AFAC, Medico International and the European Commission. British Council gave £74,976 in 2022, per the Jewish Chronicle. No current donor list.
watch: Staff told Al Jazeera that Israeli forces raided it in December 2023 and arrested two directors. Co-founder Juliano Mer-Khamis was shot dead in 2011.
records_note: The theatre posts annual reports for 2007 to 2013 and 2020, names donors in the 2013 report, lists its board, and publishes no accounts.

name: The Glucksman
funding: FY2025 income €871k: UCC subvention €428k, Arts Council €192k, other grants €13k, gifts €41k, plus shop, education and hire.
watch: Gifts (€41k) and corporate sponsors are not named. Founding donor Lewis Glucksman was a Lehman banker; banks are allowed.
records_note: No annual report; posts 2025 audited financial statements and a 2025 board list, and names University College Cork and the Arts Council as funders.

name: The Hepworth Wakefield
funding: £4.2M income in 2024-25; Arts Council England and Wakefield Council are partners. Bloomberg Philanthropies, trusts and Grand Central Rail also give.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the Supporters page names partners and funders undated, and trustees are listed.

name: The NewBridge Project
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio, Newcastle City Council, National Lottery Heritage Fund; registered charity.
watch: Artist-led community and studio space in Shieldfield; explores social justice, community food, and working-class solidarity.

name: The Polygon Gallery
funding: Opened 2017 on C$20M campaign; 2024 supporters: Canada Council, BC Arts Council, North Vancouver, BMO ($150k+), TD, RBC, Rogers, Polygon Homes, Audain endowment.
watch: Neptune Terminals (Teck/Canpotex coal-and-potash export terminal) and shipbuilder Seaspan ULC give $15k+; the Port of Vancouver does too.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2021 to 2024; the 2024 report holds financial statements, a named donor list for 2024 and the board of directors.

name: The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
funding: Registered charity The Art Gallery at Harbourfront. Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council and Toronto Arts Council; BMO Financial Group sponsors free admission.
watch: BMO Capital Markets managing director Katrina Rempel sits on the board. RBC, named earlier, is not on the current page.
records_note: Posts 14 annual reports from 2012-13 to 2025-26 naming supporters, and lists its board, but the latest shows only a draft statement of operations.

name: The Royal Standard
funding: Arts Council England, studio membership fees, non-profit project grants; artist-led registered charity.
watch: Artist-led gallery and studio complex founded in 2006 by four Liverpool artists, with 40+ studios.

name: The Whitworth
funding: University of Manchester gallery. Funders include Arts Council England, Research England, National Lottery Heritage Fund and Friends of the Whitworth; corporate: Hyundai Motor Company, Little Greene, Frieze x Deutsche Bank.
watch: In 2021 university management removed Forensic Architecture's Palestine statement and the show closed three days. In 2022, 23 artists withdrew from British Art Show 9.
records_note: Names sponsors and funders with no date; posts no annual report, accounts or board of its own, as the University of Manchester runs it.

name: TheCube Project Space
funding: National Culture and Arts Foundation (NCAF), Department of Cultural Affairs Taipei City Government; non-profit art space.
watch: Independent space in Asia for sound studies and Cold War decolonization.
